parsed.insight: That tired-but-wired feeling is so real, and the mix you've been playing may be feeding it a little without you realizing. Kingston and Sailor Song are emotionally tender and slow-burning, which can pull you deeper into reflection, while Espresso and Glow Like Dat are bright, high-energy, danceable tracks that keep your nervous system a little activated. Bouncing between those two poles — soft ache and caffeinated pop — can leave you exactly where you described: not rested, not moving, just stuck between wanting to do something and wanting to do nothing.
parsed.isoExplanation: The iso-principle means I start the playlist where you actually are — that slightly wired, mixed-tempo indie/R&B/pop zone — instead of dropping you straight into a spa. From there, each song eases valence, energy, and tempo down a notch until we arrive somewhere unmistakably calm. You're starting in a scattered, buzzing headspace, and we're moving toward Calm — settle down, quiet the noise, because after a long shift your system needs a soft landing more than another jolt. The arrival will still sound like you: indie/R&B/pop, just quieter and more spacious.

journeySongs.title: Right Side of My Neck
journeySongs.explanation: Meeting you right where Kingston left you — same warm indie ache, mid-tempo pulse, slightly wistful valence. Before shifting toward Calm, we sit with the tender, reflective mood you're already in so the transition doesn't feel forced.

journeySongs.title: Pink + White
journeySongs.explanation: Matching your starting zone with familiar R&B warmth and a gentle groove that mirrors the bounce of Espresso and Glow Like Dat without the caffeine spike. Still meeting you where you are before the settle begins.

journeySongs.title: The Only Exception
journeySongs.explanation: Holding the emotional temperature of Sailor Song — intimate, mid-energy, a little bittersweet. This is the last of the meeting-you-here songs before we start easing the noise down toward Calm.

journeySongs.title: Motion Sickness
journeySongs.explanation: First small step toward Calm: tempo stays similar but the production opens up and softens compared to Pink + White, trading rhythmic bounce for a wider, more spacious indie feel. The wired edge starts to loosen.

journeySongs.title: Self
journeySongs.explanation: Another gentle step down — lower energy and a hushed, jazzy R&B texture that's quieter than Motion Sickness. The nervous-system activation keeps dialing back toward Calm.

journeySongs.title: Ivy
journeySongs.explanation: Softer valence and less rhythmic drive than Self, with airy guitar and vocals that feel like exhaling. We're clearly moving away from wired and closer to settled.

journeySongs.title: Georgia
journeySongs.explanation: Even more restrained than Ivy — slower tempo, sparser arrangement, higher acousticness. The playlist is now firmly tilting toward quiet; the noise in your head has less to grab onto.

journeySongs.title: Godspeed
journeySongs.explanation: Landing phase begins. Just piano and voice — the most spacious R&B moment yet. Energy drops noticeably from Georgia, and the whole track feels like the room getting still around you.

journeySongs.title: Punisher
journeySongs.explanation: Deeper into Calm than Godspeed — hushed indie textures, slow tempo, almost whispered vocals. Any remaining wired edge dissolves here; this is the sound of the phone going face-down.

journeySongs.title: Nikes
journeySongs.explanation: The clearest arrival at Calm — settle down, quiet the noise in your R&B/indie world. Ambient, weightless, extremely low energy, minimal rhythm, spacious production. Nothing in this song asks anything of you. This is the quiet you were trying to give yourself when you picked up your phone instead.
